title.narrative: Improved public policies to promote the inclusion and formalization of vulnerable workers and to facilitate the implementation of sectoral OSH regulations

description.narrative:
The ILO works with Brazilian constituents to strengthen policies that promote inclusion and formalization of vulnerable workers, aligned with SDG 8 on inclusive growth, decent work, and productive employment for all.
In 2024-2025, priorities include supporting the Labour Prosecution Office (MPT), labour courts, governments, and the private sector in efforts to include traditional peoples and reduce poverty. The ILO backs the National Equal Pay Policy, Decent Work Plan for LGBTQIA+ People, and Plan for Black Youth (Plano Juventude Negra Viva), while promoting indigenous inclusion and ratification of Conventions C156, C183, and C190. It also partners with the Inter-American Centre for Knowledge Development in Vocational Training (CINTERFOR) on care training.
For 2024-2025, priorities include supporting policies by the Labour Prosecution Office (MPT), labour courts, governments, and the private sector to include traditional peoples and reduce poverty. The ILO backs the National Equal Pay Policy, Decent Work Plan for LGBTQIA+ People, and Plan for Black Youth (Plano Juventude Negra Viva), while promoting indigenous inclusion and ratification of Conventions C156, C183, and C190. It also collaborates with the Inter-American Centre for Knowledge Development in Vocational Training (CINTERFOR) on care-related training curricula.
Key efforts focus on decent work for domestic workers and improved care access for racialized and Indigenous groups. The ILO supports campaigns, dialogue, and joint strategies with social partners and civil society. These contribute to SDG 8 targets 8.5 and 8.8 by fostering equality, better working conditions, and justice.
The ILO also promotes productivity through diversification, innovation, and upgrading in labour-intensive sectors, encouraging job creation, entrepreneurship, and formalization of micro, small, and medium enterprises, with better financial access.
